subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discussion — SynapseAI next steps
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@synapseai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discussion — SynapseAI next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can move toward procurement:

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Production latency spikes at peak inference (95th pct > 900ms) across gen/chat workloads.
- Data isolation requirement for PHI-style models (must be dedicated; no multi-tenant KV cache sharing).
- Predictable unit cost for heavy embedding/semantic search pipelines.

Goals you shared:
- Reserved pool for inference (initial: 8x A100-class GPUs equivalent, target 3–6M tokens/day).
- Isolation: tenant-mapped compute + private KV cache; HIPAA-ready audit logs.
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability for reserved pool; p95 latency under 450ms for typical 512-token bursts.

Immediate next steps we proposed (and what I can own):
1) Redwood will send a short pricing/commitment worksheet and an SLA template for review — Ben will coordinate cost details (see attachment).
2) We’ll draft an initial SOW for a 90-day canary (isolation + performance validation) to validate scaling and KV cache behavior.
3) Procurement cycle: Alex to confirm procurement contact and preferred PO cadence; Redwood to provide billing profile and contract redline window.

Requested from SynapseAI by EOD Thursday:
- Target committed GPUs and monthly token estimate (ballpark is OK).
- Procurement contact + preferred contracting timeline.
- Any compliance artifacts you need from us (SOC2/DSAR specifics) so we can package them.

Attachments (sent separately): reserved-pricing-breakdown.xlsx, redwood-sla-template-v1.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync if you prefer to talk through the SOW language.

Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0147
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@synapseai.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@synapseai.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discussion — SynapseAI next steps

Chloe —

Appreciate the summary. Confirming at a high level:
- We’re leaning toward a reserved pool that maps to 8 GPUs initially, with the possibility to scale to 16 after we validate throughput in month 1.
- Primary use: multi-purpose inference (chat + embeddings). Peak windows are roughly 10–12 PT and 17–19 PT.

A few asks from procurement and engineering:
1) Can you share a sample SLO table with p50/p95 latency and the proposed credit/penalty model for missed SLOs?
2) We’ll need a short one-page summary of the isolation model for our security team (how KV/cache, network, and log separation works).
3) Procurement: point person is procurement@synapseai.com — typical PO lead time is 3–4 weeks once the SOW/price is finalized.

Happy to proceed with the canary SOW. Please route the draft SOW and the SLA template to procurement@synapseai.com and I’ll coordinate internally.

—Alex
Alex Torres
Head of AI Ops, SynapseAI
alex.torres@synapseai.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discussion — SynapseAI next steps

Quick internal note and owners:

Chloe — thanks for the recap. I’ve attached the pricing workbook and a cleaned SLA template (redwood-sla-template-v1.pdf).

Proposed internal plan:
- Ben: finalize reserved-pricing-breakdown.xlsx (ballpark commit tiers: 8, 12, 16 GPU equivalents; include overage rates and burst buckets). Owner: Ben.
- Grace (Solutions): draft one-page isolation summary + short diagram for security review. Owner: Grace.
- Chloe: finalize SOW canary draft and send to Alex + procurement. Owner: Chloe.

Canary outline (what we recommend):
- 90-day validation period, start with 8-GPU-equivalent reserved pool.
- Week 1: integration & test harness (latency baselines).
- Weeks 2–6: traffic ramp to target token/day; validate p95 budgets and KV behavior.
- Final 30 days: production-like traffic; accept/opt-in to scale.

Slack notes: I’ll queue a Solutions/Eng sync to align on test harness requirements and required telemetry (token-level tracing + KV metrics).

Attachments: reserved-pricing-breakdown.xlsx, redwood-sla-template-v1.pdf

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Alex / procurement team —

Thanks — quick update and timeline so we can align on procurement:

What you’ll receive by EOD today from Redwood:
- Draft SOW (SOW-dedicated-pool-draft.docx) covering scope, canary plan, success criteria, and acceptance testing.
- SLA template (redwood-sla-template-v1.pdf) with suggested SLOs and remediation paths.
- Pricing workbook (reserved-pricing-breakdown.xlsx) with 8/12/16 GPU-equivalent tiers and burst policy.

Requested confirmation from SynapseAI:
- Primary procurement contact for PO routing (if different from procurement@synapseai.com).
- Any mandatory vendor paperwork: W-9, vendor onboarding questionnaire link.
- Target signature date (you mentioned a 3–4 week lead time; what target date should we aim for to start the canary?).

If it helps, we can provide a 30-minute walk-through of the SOW with your security and procurement folks mid-week. Let me know what days/time work.

Thanks — attaching the three files to this thread for visibility.

Chloe Martin

chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
